methods.steps: ffmpeg -i message.gsm -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k message.mp3
methods.limits: The -b:a option sets the bitrate for libmp3lame.

methods.steps: ffmpeg -i message.gsm -c:a libmp3lame -q:a N message.mp3
methods.limits: The libmp3lame q option sets a constant quality for variable bitrate; N is a quality number.

methods.steps: sox message.gsm message.mp3
methods.limits: GSM and MP3 support are optional in SoX; MP3 writing needs the LAME library.

methods.steps: pcond scene.hdr mapped.hdr; ra_ppm mapped.hdr mapped.ppm; magick mapped.ppm preview.jpg
magick scene.hdr -colorspace sRGB preview.jpg
File > Import; choose Embed rather than Link; File > Save As; Inkscape SVG.
methods.limits: Embeds pixels rather than producing editable outlines.

methods.steps: File > Import; select the picture; Path > Trace Bitmap; save as SVG.
methods.limits: The manual says a trace suits dark silhouettes against a bright background and warns against expecting a 100% faithful representation.

methods.steps: File > Open; File > Export As > SVG.
Open the JPG; File > Export As; end the name in .cur; Export; set Hot spot X and Hot spot Y in the Windows Cursor export dialog.
In Python, import Image from PIL, call Image.open on the JPS, and call save with a file name ending in .pdf.
magick stereo.jps stereo.pdf
ffmpeg -i song.mp3 -codec:a libopencore_amrnb -b:a 12.2k -ar 8000 -ac 1 voice.amr
methods.limits: The build must be configured with --enable-libopencore-amrnb and --enable-version3.

methods.steps: sox song.mp3 -t amr-nb -C 7 -c 1 -r 8000 voice.amr
methods.limits: -C 7 is mode 7, 12.2 kbit/s; AMR-NB uses a fixed 8 kHz rate.

methods.steps: Add the MP3 with the Add button or File > Add; set Output Format to AMR; press Convert.
ffmpeg -i track.mp3 -c:a mp2 -b:a 192k track.mp2
ffmpeg -i track.mp3 -c:a libtwolame -b:a 192k track.mp2
methods.limits: The libtwolame encoder is a TwoLAME MP2 encoder wrapper.

methods.steps: Open the MP3; File > Export Audio; Format: MP2; set Bit Rate; Export.
methods.limits: Bit rates run from 16 to 384 kbps; the default is 160.

methods.app: FFmpeg transcode to an H.264/AC-3 transport stream
methods.steps: ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -f mpegts -mpegts_m2ts_mode 1 -c:a ac3 -c:v libx264 clip.m2ts
ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -c copy -mpegts_m2ts_mode 1 -f mpegts clip.m2ts
methods.limits: Copies the streams; suits an MP4 whose codecs already fit AVCHD.

methods.steps: Create a meta file: first line MUXOPT --avchd; then V_MPEG4/ISO/AVC, clip.mp4, track=1; then A_AC3, clip.mp4, track=2; set track to each stream's number in the MP4. Run tsMuxeR project.meta avchd-output.
methods.limits: Input streams must already suit the target; the muxer does not transcode.

methods.steps: ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -ar 48000 -b:v 2000k -c:a pcm_s16le -r 25 -c:v mpeg2video -ac 2 -pix_fmt yuv422p -f mxf clip.mxf
ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -an -c:v mpeg2video -b:v 4M -f mxf_opatom clip.mxf
methods.limits: The -an option drops the audio, so the file is video only.

methods.steps: magick drawing.pcx drawing.png
In Python, import Image from PIL, call Image.open on the PCX, and call save with a file name ending in .png.
